The value of the $x$-intercept of the parabola shown above is{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(-6,2)$ and passes through the point $(-7,4).$

The general standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola with vertex $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h).
$$

Substituting $(h,k)=(-6,2)$ into the above gives

$$
(y-2)^{2}=4p(x+6).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(-7,4),$ we substitute $x=-7$ and $y=4$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(4-2)^{2} & =4p(-7+6) \\ (2)^{2} & =4p\cdot (-1) \\ 4 & =-4p \\ p & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =-4(x+6).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $x$-axis, we must have $y=0.$ So, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(0+2)^{2} & =-4(x+6) \\ 4 & =-4(x+6) \\ -\frac{4}{4} & =x+6 \\ x & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercept is $-7.$
